title: Access Missouri Financial Assistance Program
sponsor: Missouri Department of Higher Education and Workforce Development

award.text: $500 to $1,700 a year at public 2-year colleges; $1,750 to $3,500 at 4-year and private schools

rules.other: Must be a Missouri resident and a U.S. citizen or permanent resident, enrolled full-time as an undergraduate at a participating Missouri school, with a Student Aid Index (SAI) of $12,000 or less. Not for theology or divinity degrees. Renewal needs a 2.5 college GPA. No bachelor's degree yet.

description: Missouri's main need-based grant. Your amount depends on your Student Aid Index from the FAFSA and the type of school you attend. There is no separate application: file the FAFSA by February 1, 2027 (priority, guaranteed award if eligible) and no later than April 1, 2027 for the 2027-28 school year.

title: Bright Flight Scholarship
sponsor: Missouri Department of Higher Education and Workforce Development

award.text: $3,000 a year for ACT 32 or higher; $1,000 a year for ACT 30 or 31 (2026 graduates, estimated)

rules.other: Must score in the top 5% of Missouri ACT or SAT takers (ACT 30 or higher for 2026 graduates; superscores accepted) by the June test date after high school graduation. Must be a Missouri resident and U.S. citizen or permanent resident, and enroll full-time at a participating Missouri school the year after graduating. Renewal needs a 2.5 college GPA.

description: A merit scholarship for Missouri students with very high ACT or SAT scores who go to college in Missouri. There is no application: the state gets your scores when you list a Missouri college on the ACT or SAT (send superscores with code 2379). It can last up to 10 semesters.

title: A+ Scholarship Program
sponsor: Missouri Department of Higher Education and Workforce Development

award.text: Unpaid tuition and general fees, up to $240 per credit hour (2026-27)

rules.other: Must attend an A+ designated high school for 2 years, sign an A+ agreement before graduating, have 95% attendance, do 50 hours of unpaid tutoring or mentoring, keep good citizenship, and score proficient on the Algebra I end-of-course exam (or meet an ACT math and GPA combination). For full-time study at a participating community college or technical school.

description: Pays tuition and general fees left after federal grants at Missouri community colleges and technical schools for students who graduate from an A+ high school and meet its goals for grades, attendance and tutoring. Ask your high school A+ coordinator early, since the requirements start in 9th grade. File the FAFSA each year.

title: Advanced Placement Incentive Grant
sponsor: Missouri Department of Higher Education and Workforce Development

rules.other: Must have scored 3 or higher on two AP math or science exams (Biology, Calculus AB or BC, Chemistry, Environmental Science, Physics 1, 2 or C, Statistics) at a Missouri public high school, and receive (or qualify for) an Access Missouri or A+ award that year. Send a paper application with your AP score report.

description: A one-time $500 bonus for Missouri students who passed two AP math or science exams in high school and now get an Access Missouri grant or A+ Scholarship in college. You apply once you are in college by mailing the application with your AP score report. The 2026-27 deadline is June 1, 2027.
